subject: Hartwell Bank — Incident Scenarios and Recovery Tolerance Mapping (RFI)
messages:
From: Sandra Liu <sandra.liu@hartwellbank.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Incident scenarios and expected RTO/RPO mapping

Neha / Marissa,

Thanks again for the quick response earlier this week. Hartwell's infrastructure and procurement teams are compiling a technical appendix for our vendor selection team and we need a concise mapping from Redwood on how different incident classes map to practical RTO/RPO outcomes. High level asks:

- For each of the following incident classes please indicate: expected target RTO (time to restore external serving), expected RPO (maximum tolerable data loss), recovery steps required, and whether the action is automated or manual:
  1) Single-host GPU failure in a Serving Cluster (hosted)
  2) Regional cloud outage affecting primary AZ (warm-standby in another region)
  3) Complete region outage requiring failover to Dedicated or Private variants
  4) Model corruption / broken weights discovered during serving
  5) KV cache loss impacting active chat sessions

- For multi-region failover: describe sequencing (control plane vs dataplane), how active requests are handled (in-flight tokens, partial responses), and whether there is an automatic model variant fallback.

- For stateful caches/embeddings: what persistence and cross-region replication options exist, and what typical RPOs are achievable for embeddings and session state?

- Please attach any recovery matrix or runbook snippets you have (we can redact anything proprietary). A short one-page matrix is perfect.

Timeline: procurement is on a tight cadence — if you can return a drafted matrix and runbook snippets by Tuesday 20 May that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Sandra Liu
Director, Platform Ops
Hartwell Bank
ops@hartwellbank.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: RFI: Incident scenarios and expected RTO/RPO mapping

Sandra —

Appreciate the clear ask. I attached a working draft (redwood-recovery-matrix-v1.xlsx) and included a short narrative below that maps the scenarios you listed to expected outcomes for our Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments.

Attachment: redwood-recovery-matrix-v1.xlsx (summary worksheet + per-scenario notes)

High-level summary (short):
- Single-host GPU failure (Hosted): automated instance replacement + cache warmup. Typical external-serving RTO: 1–3 minutes for stateless endpoints; 5–10 minutes for sessions that require KV cache rebuild (best-effort). RPO: none for input tokens; session state depends on cache TTL (default 5 min).
- AZ/regional outage (Hosted warm-standby): we route to warm-standby in <region> per policy. External-serving RTO: targeted 30s–3m for new requests once routing converges; in-flight sessions may see partial responses and may require clients to re-query. RPO: embeddings persisted to S3-backed storage with cross-region replication optional per contract (RPO can be near-zero with replication).
- Full-region failover to Dedicated/Private: depends on topology — Dedicated pools can be provisioned in multi-region mode; failover RTO targets 30m in a full failover scenario (with runbook-assisted steps).
- Model corruption: model variants and version pinning allow immediate fallback to last known-good variant; we recommend canary + automatic rollback. RTO: typically <5 min if fallback is pre-provisioned; otherwise requires model re-pull ~10–30 min depending on size.
- KV cache loss: session-level KV cache is ephemeral by default and rebuilt from recent prompts. If persistence enabled (on Dedicated/Private) we can back up to durable store — RPO depends on backup cadence (we provide incremental checkpoints).

Open clarifying Qs so we can tailor the final matrix:
1) For embeddings RPO: do you require near-zero loss (synchronous replication) or acceptable window (minutes)?
2) For chat session tolerance: do you need sticky session guarantees across regions?

I'll loop Ben for a technical addendum (runbook snippet + sequencing details). Back to you with an updated workbook by Monday AM.

Subject: RE: RFI: Incident scenarios and expected RTO/RPO mapping

Neha / Sandra —

Adding technical detail and a short runbook snippet (attached runbook-snippet.pdf) to complement Neha's summary. Key points below — call these the "practical expectations" we quote in RFPs:

1) Single-host GPU failure (Hosted):
   - Detection: health checks detect degraded NVidia driver / OOM within 30s.
   - Action: controller spins replacement pod on cluster; traffic routed to sibling replicas; prefix/KV cache is warmed from persisted checkpoints if configured.
   - External-serving RTO: 60–180s for new ephemeral requests. Session rehydration for long-lived chats depends on checkpoint cadence (default 5m -> up to 5m of session content rebuild).
   - Automation level: automated; manual ops only for persistent underlying disk issues.

2) Regional outage (warm standby):
   - Control plane: traffic steering updates via global load balancer (automated policy).
   - Data plane: model artifacts are pre-staged in standby region; KV cache is generally not replicated synchronously unless explicitly configured (we recommend async replication for embeddings).
   - In-flight requests: best-effort — we either allow clients to retry (recommended) or we surface partial responses with a retry token.
   - RTO: 30s–3m for new requests; full parity for session state requires persistence options (see below).

3) Full-region failover -> Dedicated/Private:
   - If customer has Dedicated pools across regions with replication enabled: automated failover with RTO target 30m (dependent on traffic reconfiguration and capacity warming).
   - If moving between product modes (Hosted -> Dedicated) it becomes a hands-on migration; we provide a playbook but this is not an instant switch.

4) Model corruption
   - We keep immutable model builds; operator can roll back to previous build instantly if variant is available.
   - We recommend automated canary detection and 5-minute rollback window for critical variants.

5) KV/cache/embeddings persistence
   - Embeddings: persisted to object store; we support cross-region replication. With sync-replication you can achieve near-zero RPO; async replication is typically minute-level.
   - Session KV: default ephemeral (in-memory) with checkpointing optional to durable store. With checkpointing every N minutes, RPO ~= N.

Additional operational notes:
- Sequencing: control-plane (routing) switches first; dataplane (model containers & artifacts) are served from standby if pre-staged. We avoid split-brain by enforcing single-active-write to embeddings store.
- Model fallback: automatic variant fallback requires a pre-provisioned variant in standby. We can pre-warm smaller quantized variants to reduce cold-starts.

Attachment: runbook-snippet.pdf (example play: regional-failover-sequence, cutover checklist)

If you want, we can include example timing graphs per topology in the next version.

—Ben
